summary: Task 1 is a visibility-only refactor of TelegramApiClient (private→public on four members) with byte-identical bodies, signatures, and values. Declining to add new tests is the correct call: behavior is unchanged, the four members are already exercised by the existing TelegramApiClientTest suite, and the public-surface contract will be pinned at compile time by Task 4 when TelegramSender (a different package consumer) starts calling these symbols. The three TDD anchor tests cited by the task remain meaningful coverage anchors. One pre-existing, out-of-scope gap (no negative test for requireValidTokenShape's IllegalArgumentException branch) is noted as minor.

findings.finding: No negative test exists for requireValidTokenShape's failure branch (the IllegalArgumentException thrown when the token doesn't match TOKEN_SHAPE). The happy-path test getMe_happyPath_returnsPopulatedTelegramUser passes a well-formed token, so if the entire body of requireValidTokenShape were deleted the suite would still go green for that path. This is a pre-existing gap (not introduced by Task 1) but is now slightly more relevant because the method is part of the public contract that TelegramSender will rely on.
findings.suggestion: Out of scope for Task 1 (visibility-only, AC explicitly forbids test changes). Capture as a TelegramSenderTest anchor in Task 4: when the sender invokes TelegramApiClient.requireValidTokenShape(tamperedToken) post-decrypt, it must surface IllegalArgumentException and be mapped to the appropriate AppException. Concrete assertions: StepVerifier.create(sender.send(botWithTamperedToken, ...)).expectErrorSatisfies(err -> assertThat(err).isInstanceOf(AppException.class); assertThat(((AppException) err).getCode()).isEqualTo("<expected_code>")).verify(). That single Task-4 test simultaneously pins the negative branch of requireValidTokenShape and proves the cross-class consumer wires it correctly.
findings.location: backend/src/test/java/com/botfunnel/bot/TelegramApiClientTest.java (whole file — gap, not a present-test defect)

findings.finding: CONNECT_TIMEOUT (5s, TCP-connect) has no direct behavioral test in TelegramApiClientTest. The constant is wired into HttpClient.option(ChannelOption.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MILLIS, ...) at line 58 of TelegramApiClient.java, but no test forces a TCP-connect timeout (would require a non-routable address or a deliberately stalled listener). The Netty read-timeout test (getMe_nettyReadTimeout_retriesThenReturns502TelegramUnavailable) only exercises DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT via the package-private constructor's responseTimeout parameter — it does not touch CONNECT_TIMEOUT. This is a pre-existing gap, not caused by Task 1.
findings.suggestion: Out of scope for Task 1. Do not add a connect-timeout unit test here — it would be slow and flaky (depends on socket behavior). Instead, the value's reuse-correctness is verified structurally: Task 4's TelegramSender must read CONNECT_TIMEOUT directly (per Decision 12) and a static assertion in TelegramSenderTest can pin equality, e.g. assertThat(TelegramApiClient.CONNECT_TIMEOUT).isEqualTo(Duration.ofSeconds(5)) combined with a reflection/structural check that TelegramSender's HttpClient option uses the same constant. That gives behavioral confidence without a slow socket test.

metrics.newTestsJustification: Visibility-only refactor: signatures, bodies, and values unchanged. The four promoted members continue to be exercised by the existing suite, and the public-contract pin will be enforced at compile time by Task 4's TelegramSender consumer (cross-package call site cannot compile if visibility regresses).

details.reasoning: If the body of requireValidTokenShape is deleted, the test still passes (token is well-formed; the deleted check would have done nothing on this happy path anyway). The test exercises the call site, but does not pin the validator's logic. This is a known pre-existing gap, surfaced as a minor finding above.

If isTransient is gutted to always return false, the Retry.filter rejects every signal, the very first 503 propagates immediately, and mockServer.getRequestCount() == 4 fails (would be 1). The assertion on request count and on the BAD_GATEWAY/telegram_unavailable mapping both depend on isTransient correctly recognizing 5xx as transient.

If the ReadTimeoutException branch in isTransient is removed, retry never engages on the read-timeout and request count is 1 instead of 4 — test fails. Also confirms the response-timeout plumbing path (custom 200ms override via the package-private constructor exercises the same wiring code that DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT flows through in the public constructor).

requireValidTokenShape(String).gap: No negative test asserting IllegalArgumentException for a malformed token. Surfaced as a minor finding above; appropriate fix is in Task 4's TelegramSenderTest.

isTransient(Throwable).gap: No direct test for the IOException branch or the TimeoutException (java.util.concurrent) branch in isolation. Acceptable: those branches are reached via the WebClient/Netty stack and are already shaken by the retry-exhausted scenarios above. Not a Task-1 concern.

All other tests (use the public constructor at TelegramApiClientTest:41, which threads DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT implicitly)
DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT.gap: Value (10s) is not asserted directly (no assertThat(DEFAULT_RESPONSE_TIMEOUT).isEqualTo(Duration.ofSeconds(10))). Acceptable for Task 1 — the value is a compile-time constant and the timeout-wiring code path is exercised. Task 4 can add a structural assertion if useful.

coveredBy: All tests (constant is wired into HttpClient at construction time for every test)
CONNECT_TIMEOUT.gap: No behavioral test forces a TCP-connect timeout. Surfaced as a minor finding; not appropriate to fix in Task 1 (would be slow/flaky). Best addressed structurally in Task 4 via equality assertion + verification that TelegramSender reads the same constant.

pyramidBalance.note: TelegramApiClientTest uses MockWebServer for HTTP-layer fidelity, making these effectively narrow integration tests against a fake server. Distribution is appropriate for the SUT (a thin reactive HTTP client). Integration/E2E coverage for the connect/disconnect flow lives outside this file (BotService tests, controller tests) and is unaffected by Task 1.
